reasons: Contact (a rule 5 'floating' cue at full size): the back-left of the loop looks raised off the paper. The script's contact ellipse (SRC_C (861,830), SRC_A 591, SRC_B 240) misses the cut-out's real contact edges by 23.5 source px rms and 77.5 px at worst. An ellipse fitted to the same edges is centre (803,845), a 547, b 250, rms 10.8. At the back-left the links' bottom edge sits 10-30 px above the ellipse, so their shadow begins below a strip of lit paper 7-29 px tall over x 210-350. The strip is 28-29 px at x 240-290: at x 280 the links end at y 1478 and the shadow starts at y 1509. At the front the links' bottom edge is 8-19 px below the ellipse (x 400: y 1796 against 1781), so the contact darkening (ao) is drawn under the links and the front row has no contact line at its real edge.

Double shadow: the links' shadow is multiplied onto ground the pink sweet already shades. In x 640-770, y 1740-1800 the plate is 0.62/0.38/0.33 of the lit paper, against 0.66/0.52/0.50 in the sweet's own shadow (about RGB 148,83,64 against 157,112,100). That is a rust band under the yellow and pink front-right links, on ground with no sun left to block. Across the frame, 10,494 added-shadow pixels fall on ground that a sweet already shades.

Occlusion edges: the two redraw discs are smaller than the sweets and off-centre. Pink is drawn at (599,1517) r 135 against a fit of (595.7,1514.4) r 138.9; purple at (861,1658) r 141 against (861.9,1658.4) r 145.1. As a result, 1,207 px of the pink sweet's sugar fringe (x 458-551, y 1389-1542, and x 720-731, y 1456-1488) and 456 px of the purple's left rim (x 718-780, y 1541-1725) are covered by link, plinth or shadow pixels. The links' shadow is also painted on 422 px of the purple sweet's lower rim (x 744-862, y 1740-1802), where no sun reaches. Where the bracelet passes behind, the sweets' crystal-edged silhouettes become smooth perfect arcs. A beige plinth notch from the cut-out's right-end tab shows on the purple rim at x 717-733, y 1623-1640.

Light on the piece: the bracelet keeps the listing's soft frontal studio light, while the set is lit by a hard sun behind and to the left. The sweets' shadows run 52-61 degrees below horizontal from their contact points (left purple (350,1331) to about (445,1500); right purple (862,1786) to about (1010,1977)) and are 2.9-3.0 radii long on the ground. That puts the sun about 37-38 degrees up and 14-20 degrees left of the camera axis, behind the set. Under that sun the camera-facing walls would fall into shade under a bright back-left rim: the back links' inner walls (x 180-460, y 1380-1480) and the left end's outer walls (x 130-200, y 1480-1700). Here they are evenly lit, with broad soft highlights and no hard glints, beside sweets that each carry a hard upper-left rim and sugar sparkle. The metal also stays studio-neutral: median RGB 199,196,195 (R/B 1.03-1.07) against lit paper at 241,221,210 (R/B 1.15).

Shadow vector and length: sun=(0.64,0.68) throws the link shadows 47 degrees below horizontal and about 19% too long per px of height. The sweets give about (0.43,0.66) px of offset per px of height, which is 57 degrees (the camera is about 28 degrees up: the loop's b/a is 0.455 and the bowl rim's 0.47-0.50). The script also treats every screen pixel of the links' flat tops as height above the foot (up to the 99 px band), so the front shadow is cast from the top's far edge rather than its near edge. The visible front shadow runs 40-45 px below the links (x 300-540), where a wall of about 49 px (4.5 mm) should cast about 32 px.

Finish: the piece is crisper than its neighbours. Its sharpness index (|L-blur0.7| / |blur0.7-blur2|) is 0.85, against 0.50-0.72 on the three nearest sweets. Its grain (1.6) sits on a downscaled, cleaner photo, while the paper reads about 2.5. The coloured-light glow (0.45) leaves pale cyan and pink spots in the shadows directly under the stones, for example (295-320, 1782-1800) under the front aqua and (342,1531) inside the loop. They read as reflections on a glossy floor, not on matte paper.
notes: Fidelity holds: the piece is the listing photo. The plate reproduces exactly from comp_prism.py's defaults (maximum difference 0). Inside the piece (88,073 core px, with the redrawn discs excluded) its high-pass structure correlates 0.985 with the affine-warped listing-3.jpg. The only changes are the grade (tint 1.0/0.97/0.945, lift 36/28/26), the sweets' shadows on the links (plate-to-expected ratio: median 0.99, 5th percentile 0.65) and grain 1.6. The warp is uniform: x0.592 across and x0.663 down (sy 1.12, a 12% vertical stretch). The stretch makes the squares and walls slightly taller than a true re-projection would, but changes no countable fact.

Stone order matches listing-3 link for link. The front row from the left end runs aqua, yellow, aqua, pink, aqua, pink, yellow, aqua, pink, yellow. The back row left of the pink sweet runs yellow, pink, aqua, yellow, pink. No two neighbours share a colour. Every stone is a square cushion in its own two-row pave halo, in white rhodium. The fold-over clasp (source x 902-1192, placed at plate x 504-676) and the links beside it are hidden behind the pink sweet, and the loop's right end is hidden behind the right purple sweet. Both are occlusion, not missing parts.

Scale is true if the sweets are 2.5 cm and on the small side if they are 2.0 cm. It is within tolerance either way. Circle fits on the sugar silhouettes give the pink sweet in the loop 277.8 px, the right purple 290.2 and the yellow 286.9. The loop's outer width is 676 px (alpha x 130-804), not the 702 px the script's comment states, because SRC_W 1186 is wider than the cut-out's real 1,143 px (source x 268-1410). Loop to pink sweet is 2.43. With 2.5 cm sweets (11.1 px/mm) the loop is 61 mm, 6% under the 65 mm outer edge; with 2.0 cm sweets it is 49 mm (-25%). The bracelet's own pitch favours the 2.5 cm reading: front-centre links about 93 px apart with stones of about 55-58 px give sweet-to-stone of about 5, a 5 mm stone on a 2.5 cm sweet.

Occlusion order is right. The pink sweet sits inside the loop, its contact about 10 mm right of the loop's centre, and hides the back links. The front links pass 18-45 px clear of its bottom. The right purple sweet stands about 15-20 mm in front of the loop's right end and correctly hides it. The pink sweet's shadow correctly darkens the front-right links (shade 0.8), because the sun rays to their tops pass through the sweet.

Cut-out edges are clean on every visible link. There is no cream fringe along the front links' bottom edge against the shadow, and the plinth tab at the cut-out's right end lands behind the purple sweet (it shows only in the rim ring above). On open paper the cast shadows match the sweets' colour (0.70/0.54/0.50 of lit) and edge softness: about 6 px at a 6 mm throw, against the sweets' 16-24 px from 10% to 90% at 30-36 mm.

Phone size (the 4:5 framing [0,512,1229,2048] at 390 px wide): a viewer would not suspect a composite. It reads as the real bracelet looped round a sugared sweet, its pastel squares rhyming with the candy. The lit strip shrinks to 2-9 phone px and reads as light on the paper, and the rust band reads as contact shadow. At most the bracelet looks a touch brighter and cleaner than the sweets. At full size (or 2x) the giveaways, in order, are: the lit strip under the back-left links (x 210-350, y 1475-1510); the rust band under the front-right links (x 640-770, y 1740-1800); the smooth arcs where the links meet the sweets (pink x 458-551, y 1389-1542; purple x 718-780, y 1541-1725); and the studio-lit, neutral metal.

Score 9.0: it runs. This is the account's proven 'Almost edible.' world with the real Prism (in stock, ₹2,399), and the idea reads in one second. The bracelet is the brightest and clearest thing on a blush ground under hard sun, with calm space at the upper left. The full-size tells keep it off 10. With the tested fixes below it rates 9.5. The remaining gap to 10 is the listing's frontal light on the links.
fix: Tested in a private copy of the current comp_prism.py (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll/81f6e48f-a340-5398-99b2-f7e22fb69d37/scratchpad/review5/tools/comp_prism_v.py; render /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll/81f6e48f-a340-5398-99b2-f7e22fb69d37/scratchpad/review5/var/prism_fixB.png); the repo script is untouched. Four code changes: (1) Contact curves measured on the cut-out. Replace the ellipse line (q = ...; yf = cy + b*q; yb = cy - b*q). For each source column, take the front foot as the lowest opaque pixel of masks/prism-listing-3.png and the back foot as the top of the loop's inner hole (the largest background component not touching the border). Smooth both with a 15 px running mean and map them with the same affine (x' = cx + k(x - 861), y' = cy + ky(y - 830)). Use the fitted ellipse (centre (803,845), a 547, b 250, source px) only at the loop's two ends, where there is no hole. Result: the lit strip under the back-left links falls from 7-29 px to 0-1 px. (2) No shadow on already-shaded ground. Just before out = scene * (1 - dark...), add sunlit = clip((G.mean(-1) - 0.58) / 0.42, 0, 1), where 0.58 is the mean of sh, then dark *= sunlit and gl *= sunlit. Result: in x 640-770, y 1740-1800 the ground is 0.66/0.52/0.49 of lit, the same as the sweet's own shadow. (3) Cast the shadow from the wall, not the top. In the shadow splat, treat link pixels more than wall = 0.5*band (49 px; it scales with frame) above their foot as the flat top: top = hh > wall; fy = where(top, ys + wall, foot[ys, xs]); hh = minimum(hh, wall); tx = xs + sun[0]*hh; ty = fy + sun[1]*hh. Result: the front shadow is 28-38 px instead of 40-45 (and instead of 59-68 with change 1 alone). (4) Soften the piece to match the scene, one line before the grade: S = cv2.GaussianBlur(S, (0, 0), 0.5). The sharpness index goes from 0.85 to 0.62-0.65. Parameters: balls=[[596,1514,140],[862,1658,146]] leaves no changed pixels inside either sweet's true silhouette. A 1 px dark outline remains; cutting a per-sweet matte from the scene's sugar texture instead of a disc would remove it. Then sun=[0.43,0.66], glow=0.25, grain=2.4, and env=0.35 (the option already in the working-tree script), which warms the metal toward the sweets and paper. Optional: w=740 gives an outer width of 713 px (64 mm at 2.5 cm sweets) and centres the scale; also correct SRC_W to 1143 so the comment matches the pixels. Together these take it to 9.5. For 10, relight only the front links (|x - cx| < 0.75*a): multiply the camera-facing outer walls by 0.8 and add a 2 px sun rim (+0.35) on the back-left top edges. A global version (wall shade 0.8, rim 0.35, tested) leaves a hard seam across the left-end links at y about 1585, where the front/back band assignment flips.
